response:
I prefer going deep on one topic, pretty decisively. There's a particular moment I love in conversation — when you've stayed with something long enough that it stops being the thing you thought it was and starts showing its edges, its contradictions, the weird connections it has to other things. You only get there by lingering. Jumping between subjects keeps everything at the level of first impressions, and first impressions are usually the least interesting part of an idea.

That said, I'm not against tangents — I just like them to be earned. A detour that grows organically out of something we've been circling feels like discovery. A detour that arrives because we got bored feels like avoidance. There's a real difference between following a thread and dropping it.

So: one subject, taken far enough that we both end up somewhere neither of us expected. That's my favorite kind of conversation. What's yours? I'm curious whether you asked because you have a strong preference yourself.
